Subject: Telehealth data retention: escrow vs redaction options

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance and legal teams: PilotCare needs clarity on two things for our telehealth transcripts and clinician notes that flow through Redwood: 1) whether Redwood supports a contractual data escrow (we would like a snapshot of data at defined intervals for our records), and 2) what redaction/pseudonymization approaches you support for PII/PHI if retention windows are restricted by regulation.

Specifically: we need to understand whether escrow snapshots can be limited to field-level exports (no free text) and whether Redwood can provide automated redaction at ingestion and on-demand redaction for already-processed tokens (e.g., purge/kvs). Also attaching a preliminary data map for context.

Can your team propose 2–3 options with operational trade-offs (latency, cost, auditability)? Our legal ops prefers short bullets with recommended SLOs.

Best,
Paola Ruiz
Head of Compliance, PilotCare Health

Subject: Re: Telehealth data retention: escrow vs redaction options

Paola —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the data map. Quick summary before we loop in detailed SRE/security: yes, we can support both (A) a contractual escrow export and (B) multiple redaction options. Below are 3 pragmatic options with the trade-offs you requested. We'll follow up with a short PDF and an implementation checklist by EOD Monday.

Option 1 — Field-level escrow + minimal retention on Redwood hosted runtime
- What: Periodic encrypted field-level exports (CSV/Parquet) for fields you designate; no free-text columns included.
- Operational: Exports taken nightly (or hourly if needed) to an S3-compatible escrow bucket controlled by PilotCare (you provide endpoint and ACLs).
- Trade-offs: Lowest risk for data leakage; you maintain canonical copy. Slightly higher cost due to export frequency and storage, minimal runtime latency impact.
- Auditability: Full manifest + checksums; we can provide a signed delivery receipt.

Option 2 — Full ingest + on-ingest redaction + rolling retention window
- What: Accept full payloads, apply deterministic field-level redaction/pseudonymization at ingest (names/SSNs/emails replaced with consistent tokens), keep only pseudonymized output in long-term store, purge raw KV caches after retention window (e.g., 30/90/365 days).
- Operational: Faster developer experience (no separate export pipeline), supports debugging via reversible token maps (if you opt-in), but reversibility requires additional controls (KMS-wrapped lookup).
- Trade-offs: Better for live features needing identifiers; requires careful key management and stricter audit controls.

Option 3 — Ephemeral runtime + on-demand redaction + escrow on request
- What: Minimal retention in-host (short-term caches only), no long-term storage of transcripts by default. Escrow performed on-demand (for legal/clinical needs) as a one-off export. Redaction performed pre-export or as a post-export sanitized copy.
- Operational: Lowest long-term data footprint; best for strict-regulatory customers who cannot accept stored transcripts. Higher operational lead time for exports and slower incident debugging.

Next steps: Monica — can you draft a one-page checklist mapping these options to our current product features and estimated SLOs? Naomi / Neha: please review for SOC2 evidence and deletion timelines. Paola — happy to jump on a short call Monday to walk through.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Principal Product Manager — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Telehealth data retention: escrow vs redaction options

Hi all —

Draft checklist (high level) attached as PDF. Highlights for Legal Ops:
- Escrow: supports S3-compatible endpoints; retention and lifecycle controlled by PilotCare. We sign export manifests and rotate export keys monthly.
- Redaction: two patterns supported out-of-the-box — deterministic tokenization (non-reversible unless you supply a wrapped KMS key) and irreversible masking.
- Purge semantics: We expose a purge API with three scopes: runtime caches, indexed transcripts, and audit logs. Purge requests are asynchronous; SLA 48–72 hours for full deletion from all indexes and caches (longer if export/backup windows overlap).

Risks/notes:
- If you require escrow snapshots that include clinician free-text, that increases PII surface and will require additional legal review and an elevated security posture (HSM-backed keys, higher retention monitoring).
- For incident investigations we recommend a short reversible tokenization window (e.g., reversible for 14 days) then automatic switch to irreversible masking.

I'll coordinate a one-hour call with our SRE and security leads if you want to review the purge execution flow.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Monica —

Thanks for the clear checklist. A few clarifying Qs from Legal Ops:
1) Can Redwood include a tamper-evident manifest and notarization for escrow deliveries? We prefer SHA256 checksums plus a signed manifest.
2) Is the 48–72 hour purge SLA inclusive of backups/replication? We need assurance that exported backups can be flagged and removed.
3) For deterministic tokenization that is reversible, can PilotCare hold the KMS key? We prefer that to avoid Redwood being able to re-identify patients.

If you can confirm those points in writing, we can progress contract language. We still want a short technical call to validate the purge path end-to-end.

Regards,
Paola

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Telehealth data retention: escrow vs redaction options

Paola / Legal Ops —

Short answers below to help with contract drafting:

1) Tamper-evident manifests: yes — we provide SHA256 checksums for each export and sign the manifest with a rotating RSA key; we can include the public key in the contract and provide a notarized delivery receipt.

2) Purge SLA scope: the 48–72 hour window covers our primary indexes and runtime caches. Backups are excluded by default because of snapshot windows; however, we can add a contractual clause to flag and remove affected backups within a specified remediation window (typical add-on: 7–14 days depending on backup retention policy). We will document the RTO/RPO implications in the contract.

3) Customer-held KMS: supported. PilotCare may supply an external KMS/HSM endpoint or provide an encrypted wrapping key; reversible tokens require a wrapped key that only you control. If you hold the key, Redwood cannot reverse tokens.

Operational notes:
- For reversible tokenization we recommend an audit log of all re-ids and a two-person approval flow.
- For escrow exports that include free text, we advise adding a pre-export sanitization step (automated NER redaction with manual review) to reduce PHI leakage risk.

If agreeable, Monica / Michael can we schedule a 30-minute call Wednesday to validate the purge flow and run through a sample export from a staging tenant?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
